zh.title: 星宇航空蟬聯SKYTRAX五星認證 獲全球最整潔航空第一名
zh.summary: 星宇航空獲2026年SKYTRAX五星認證，並奪全球最整潔航空公司第一名。
body: 星宇航空於2026年9月18日在英國倫敦舉行的2026年SKYTRAX全球航空公司大獎頒獎典禮中，獲頒五星航空認證，連續第二年獲得該項最高榮譽評級。同時，星宇航空也在本次評比中奪得「全球最整潔航空公司」第一名。
根據星宇航空說明，SKYTRAX五星評級依據現場稽核與綜合評比，涵蓋機場服務、客艙環境、機上服務及餐飲品質等多項面向。而「全球最整潔航空公司」獎項則聚焦旅客接觸的客艙環境清潔，包含座艙、座椅、餐桌、地毯與廁所等維護狀況。
星宇航空執行長翟健華表示，能連續兩年獲得五星認證並獲選最整潔航空公司第一名，是對全體員工服務品質與細節堅持的肯定。SKYTRAX執行長普雷斯德（Edward Plaisted）亦恭喜星宇航空獲得全球最整潔航空公司第一名，並肯定其為各艙等旅客提供的高品質服務。

en.title: Starlux Airlines Retains SKYTRAX 5-Star Rating and Wins World's Cleanest Airline Award
en.summary: Starlux Airlines retained its SKYTRAX 5-Star rating and was named World's Cleanest Airline in London.
body: Starlux Airlines received its 5-Star Airline certification for the second consecutive year at the 2026 SKYTRAX World Airline Awards in London on September 18, 2026. The carrier was also awarded first place as the World's Cleanest Airline.

The SKYTRAX 5-Star rating is based on audits and evaluations covering airport services, cabin environment, onboard service, and catering quality. The World's Cleanest Airline category focuses on cabin cleanliness, including seats, tray tables, carpets, and lavatories.

Starlux Airlines Chief Executive Officer Glenn Chai stated that retaining the 5-Star rating and winning the cleanliness category reflects the dedication of the airline's staff. SKYTRAX Chief Executive Officer Edward Plaisted congratulated the carrier on its achievements and high service standards across all cabin classes.

zh.title: 美海軍為F/A-18超級大黃蜂引入Auto-GCAS系統
zh.summary: 美海軍採用Auto-GCAS系統；超級大黃蜂增防撞保護
body: Simple Flying於2026年9月19日報導：「The US Navy is finally bringing Auto-GCAS to its F/A-18 fleet, adding a critical layer of protection against potentially fatal ground collisions.」，顯示美國海軍將為F/A-18超級大黃蜂艦隊引入自動地面防撞系統。
文章標題指出美海軍等待十年才讓超級大黃蜂飛行員獲得空軍救命的Auto GCAS，凸顯該技術採用的漫長時程。
Auto-GCAS系統將為海軍飛行員提供關鍵防護層，防範可能致命的撞地意外。

en.title: US Navy to equip F/A-18 Super Hornets with Auto-GCAS ground collision avoidance system
en.summary: US Navy adopts Auto-GCAS for Super Hornets; adds ground collision protection
body: Simple Flying reported on September 19, 2026, that the US Navy is finally bringing Auto-GCAS to its F/A-18 fleet, adding a critical layer of protection against potentially fatal ground collisions.

The article's headline states that the Navy waited a decade to give Super Hornet pilots the Air Force's life-saving Auto GCAS, underscoring the extended timeline for adopting the Air Force's life-saving Auto GCAS.
The automatic ground collision avoidance system will provide a critical protection layer for Navy pilots against potential fatal ground collisions for its fleet, according to the report.
